key_insight: Parallel multi-agent LLM systems are only faster when their critical-path savings exceed hidden re-exploration and alignment overheads.
engineering_relevance: SquidAgent offers a practical scheduling rule for choosing when to parallelize agent workflows, making multi-agent orchestration more efficient for real-world AI systems.
method: Estimate layer costs in predicted output tokens instead of wall-clock time.
Fork workers from the orchestrator session to avoid re-exploration of shared context.
Use a pre-generated shared convention block to bound alignment overhead before execution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 2.2× mean throughput improvement and 2.6× mean wall-time speedup over Claude Code, plus a 2.0× throughput gain over the strongest multi-agent baseline.
watch_item: The token-based cost model and shared-convention setup may require careful calibration to remain reliable across tasks and model families.
